transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-13
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Cho (Redwood SE), Karen Li (CTO, RiverMark), Diego Morales (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (SRE)
Shared artifacts: https://redwood.jira/benchmarks/rivermark-ttft (benchmark spreadsheet), https://drive.company/rivermark/poc-notes (POC notes)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on TTFT and streaming behavior. Reviewed recent benchmark numbers, dug into kernel choices and sequence-length effects, agreement to run additional kernel sweeps and a staged benchmark with real traffic profile. Action items and dates captured.

Topics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, sequence length distribution and KV cache behavior, kernel selection (cuBLAS / Triton / custom fused kernels), batching, percentile SLOs, Dedicated vs Hosted options for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, um Elena and I from Redwood, and from RiverMark we've got Karen, Diego, Priya, right?
[00:14] Karen: yep that's right, thanks Samir. we've been looking forward to the numbers.
[00:20] Elena: cool, i'll kick off with the latest TTFT sweep we ran monday night. i put the sheet in the shared link, it's the g5x2 and g6a2 runs, 256, 512, 1k token sequences, streaming toggled.
[00:35] Diego: sorry quick Q - our production median seq len is about 180 but we do have an 8% tail above 800 tokens when users request transaction histories.
[00:48] Priya: and our burst profile is 40 rps for short periods, then drops to 5 rps. p95 latency target is 200ms for first token ideally.
[01:02] Samir: ok good context. so in the numbers we saw: g6a2 improved average token generation latency by ~12% but TTFT didn't move much unless streaming was enabled.
[01:18] Elena: right, because TTFT is dominated by model load / kernel startup on some paths. when streaming is on we pump the first chunk earlier, so you see a ~30-50ms improvement in TTFT for 256-512 seqs. for 1k sequences the benefit is larger since amortized compilation overhead is different.
[01:40] Karen: are we sure that compilation overhead is live on hosted? i thought Redwood pre-warms kernels for pinned model versions?
[01:52] Samir: good point - for the Dedicated pilot we can pin and pre-warm, hosted will have more variability. the runs we shared were cold-ish to simulate out-of-canary edge cases; we can run pre-warm profiles too.
[02:08] Diego: the kernel choice question - you mentioned cuBLAS vs triton path, can you clarify?
[02:16] Elena: yeah so our runtime picks kernels based on architecture. for some attention sizes the cuBLAS matmul path is faster, for others our fused-triton kernels (i'll call them triton/custom here) win. the heuristic sometimes mis-classifies at longer sequences which raises token latency.
[02:33] Diego: hmm that matches our run of open-source runner where specific seq lengths flip the kernel choice and latency spikes.
[02:42] Elena: exactly. we'll run a per-layer per-kernel benchmark to show the flip points.
[02:52] Samir: also want to flag KV cache behavior - prefix caching helps for requests that reuse context, but for your 8% long-history requests we saw memory pressure causing minor eviction which can bump TTFT if we need to repopulate.
[03:08] Priya: is that a config we can tune? we have racks with more memory but we'd rather not overprovision.
[03:16] Elena: yes it's tunable: cache window, shard sizing, and eviction policy. for Dedicated we'll recommend a profile that nails your tail while keeping cost reasonable.
[03:26] Karen: any notes on batching? we worry about p95 tail increases when batching for cost reductions.
[03:34] Samir: batching is a lever - we do continuous batching with a latency cap. you can set a max wait time for the batch and a max batch size. we've been running with a 6ms wait cap for these runs which keeps p95 within target for median seqs but hurts the long tail.
[03:50] Diego: can we do dynamic batching based on routing policies? like route premium traffic to low-wait queues?
[03:58] Elena: yes that's in the routing policy - you can prioritize by token budget, customer tier, or path. for the pilot we suggested pinning the critical routes to dedicated low-latency nodes.
[04:10] Karen: what about streaming vs chunk size? we saw weird artifacting when chunk size was too small.
[04:18] Elena: small chunks reduce TTFT but increase per-token overhead. there's a sweet spot - for your workload: 64-128 token chunk sizes gave best first token while keeping overall token rate ok in our tests.
[04:33] Samir: quick note on metrics - the benchmark spreadsheet has columns: TTFT cold, TTFT warm, token latency avg, p95 token, memory usage, kernel path. check tabs 'g5x2-stream' and 'g6a2-nostream'.
[04:50] Diego: got it, i'll review later.
[05:00] Karen: can you remind us what you mean by cold vs warm in these runs?
[05:05] Elena: cold means no pre-warmed kernels and first requests pay for JIT/compilation. warm means we've run a warmup sequence and have kernels resident and KV cache primed. production should be mostly warm for pinned model versions.
[05:20] Priya: we're considering Hosted first, then Dedicated if our SLOs need it - what tradeoffs did you see?
[05:29] Samir: hosted is fastest to get started but variable at tail. Dedicated gives you control to pin model versions, pre-allocate memory, and set autoscaling rules. cost is higher but predictable and better for your p95 target if you need strict SLAs.
[05:44] Diego: regarding kernel selection automation - can you expose heuristics so we can reproduce locally? we want to match local profiling to your cloud runs.
[05:53] Elena: yes we'll export the kernel heuristic logs. they're in the debug trace but we can surface a simplified mapping table per model and seq length.
[06:05] Samir: quick aside - we noticed quantization profile impacted kernel choice; 4-bit quantization sometimes flips to a different attention kernel so please note Q4 runs separately.
[06:20] Karen: did you do Q4 in the latest sheet?
[06:24] Elena: we did not - these were fp16 baseline. Q4 runs are next in queue.
[06:30] Diego: ok can we prioritize Q4 since cost matters for us?
[06:34] Samir: yes we'll bump Q4 runs up the list.
[06:38] Elena: for next steps on benchmarking, i propose: 1) run TTFT Q4 and fp16 for g6a2 256/512/1k, 2) per-kernel breakdown, 3) streaming chunk sweep 32/64/128 tokens.
[06:53] Karen: sounds good. one more thing - security for Dedicated: KMS integration and audit logs are must-haves. how soon can you share docs?
[07:03] Samir: i sent the security pack last week but i'll re-share the specific KMS doc and our SOC2 audit summary. expect that by EOD today.
[07:12] Priya: also need network design for VPC peering if we go Dedicated in staging.
[07:18] Elena: we'll include a sample diagram and firewall rules in the doc set.
[07:24] Diego: can we talk about a tactical benchmark run on staging? here's what i'd like: 1k tokens, streaming enabled, real traffic replay of 10 minutes at 40 rps burst, measure TTFT distribution and p95.
[07:38] Samir: yep that's doable. we'll need the traffic replay artifact or access to a replay bucket. Diego, can you share that?
[07:44] Diego: yes i'll upload to the shared drive after this call.
[07:48] Samir: great. we'll schedule the run for next tuesday assuming artifacts are in.
[07:54] Elena: timeline-wise, I'll have the kernel breakdown by friday (2027-07-15), Samir will run the Q4 TTFT sweep by saturday (2027-07-16), and the staged benchmark tentatively 2027-07-20.
[08:10] Karen: that's aggressive but fine.
[08:14] Priya: one small thing - how are you reporting observer-level traces? we want to link to our internal Jaeger traces.
[08:22] Elena: we can export trace spans with standard OpenTelemetry format; we'll show mapping of Redwood spans to your trace events.
[08:30] Samir: ok moving on - found a small anomaly: g5x2 streaming run at 512 tokens had a 2% outlier at 1.2s TTFT. looking at logs it was a kernel fallback due to memory fragmentation.
[08:45] Diego: memory fragmentation? can that happen on Dedicated too?
[08:49] Elena: yes but it's less likely if we pre-allocate and pin. also fragmentation can be reduced by choosing a slightly larger shard size or changing allocator settings. we'll include suggested configs.
[09:02] Karen: any risk to multi-tenancy? these runs are single-tenant but we might co-locate some non-critical workloads.
[09:10] Samir: multi-tenant increases noisy neighbor risk; Dedicated avoids that by default. for hosted we mitigate with QoS and cgroup isolation but it's not as strict as dedicated hardware.
[09:22] Diego: what about model fallbacks - if you lose a node, does Redwood fall back to a smaller quantized variant?
[09:28] Elena: yes routing policies can fallback to compatible variants. we recommend setting an explicit compatibility map so fallbacks are predictable.
[09:36] Priya: can the fallback preserve streaming sessions? we can't drop client streams mid-conversation.
[09:43] Samir: streaming handoff is tricky - we try to drain existing streams on the old node and start new streams on fallback; there's a small window where clients may see latency increase but not a silent drop. we'll document the behavior.
[09:58] Karen: ok any blockers from our side? Diego said he'd upload the replay; what else?
[10:05] Diego: nothing else, i'll also export a p95 target document and sample user session.
[10:12] Samir: great - recap of action items below.
[10:18] Elena: quick FYI - i'll include an annotated kernel mapping tab in the spreadsheet so you can see which kernel was active for each step.
[10:29] Karen: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[10:33] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the staged run.
[10:38] Priya: thanks.
